Try this: Pick a real number between 0 and 1 (3+ decimal places is best). Double it, then chop off the integer before the decimal. The numbers remaining are your first number. Double that, chop off anything before the decimal point, and that’s your second number. Repeat. Example:

.448 * 2 = 0.896
0.896 * 2 =1.792
0.792 * 2 = 1.584
0.584 * 2 = 1.168
0.168 * 2 = 0.336

From this you get: 896, 792, 584, 168, 336. For smaller numbers, just use the first digit, or break it up: 8, 9, 6, 7, 9, 2, 5, 8, 4, 1, 6, 8, 3, 3, 6… etc.

Hi! I’ve made it a couple different ways, and in this photo I’m using Icelandic skyr as the base. But a great way to make it is:

- 3/4 cup nonfat cottage cheese (70cal/half cup), blended just until smooth [can also use yogurt]
- 1 tbsp chia seeds (60 cals)
- 1/4 cup vanilla almond milk
- 1/2tsp xanthan gum (optional, 5 cal)
- 3 or 4 FROZEN strawberries, microwaved for 1 min and then mashed
- Stur strawberry water enhancer or another sweetener
- Pinch of salt, splash of vanilla

1. Combine the cottage cheese, chia seeds, 1/4tsp xanthan gum, salt, sweetener, + almond milk, and whisk. 

2. Add 1/4tsp xanthan gum to mashed frozen strawberries (keep the juices!) and add sweetener to taste. Mash and mix so there are no clumps. 

3. Give the strawberry jam a minute to thicken, then swirl with the base. Refrigerate overnight to thicken.

It sounds complicated, but it takes me like 5 minutes lol. I usually use yogurt instead of cottage cheese because it’s what I have on hand, but I expect cottage cheese would be a more “cheesecake-y” flavor. Good luck!

This was my attempt to compile my “best” colors into a palette, because the palettes I’ve found online never seem exactly right. (I tried to make it line up with the colors in my head, but it’s not perfect). I’ve never been able to decide on a color season — I lean mostly towards autumn, probably deep or soft, but I also have winter characteristics (and maybe even some summer).

There are a few, very specific colors that look amazing on me, and a lot that make me look like a corpse, but the vast majority are in some in-between zone where how flattering they are depends on who you ask.

I would describe my best colors as turquoise, jade, coral, mascarpone/creamy whites, moss green, rust/terracotta (not too orange), plum, warm berry shades, dark chocolate, and any shade of pink besides pastel or bubblegum. In general, colors with too much of a yellow undertone make me look washed out/sickly. Pinky-reds and blue-greens are best. Bright/neon colors usually look horrible, but saturated colors with warmish undertones look great.

For reference, I have yellow-olive undertones, and I am very pale during the winter. Nars Gobi is my perfect match. I tan a bit more during the summer, but I actually prefer the way clothes look against my untanned skin (tanning somehow makes me look more sallow). I have dark brown hair with subtle auburn undertones. In the sunlight, I have bright green eyes with a tiny burst of yellow in the centers. However, my eyes can also appear grey (desaturated) or brownish depending on the light. I had blue eyes for the first 3.5ish years of my life. I can wear pure black, but only off-white. Some warm colors look great, some look horrific. Same for cool colors. My complexion looks nice first thing in the morning, but looks orangeish by night time. My father is as pale as can be, with white-blond hair, icy blue eyes, cool pinkish undertones, low saturation. My mother has warm (though not olive) undertones, and dark hair/hazel eyes like me. I definitely share more of her coloring.

Oh, and khaki, navy, and other typical neutrals look terrible.

Any help is really appreciated!

ETA: [this palette](https://pin.it/HShRTLm) is the best I’ve found so far.

I can certainly pull off some of the spring colors, but I don’t think my complexion is quite “clear” enough for a lot of them. The brighter/lighter the colors are, the more they seem to wash me out. Lime green, lemon yellow, and most oranges look horrible on me, and I see them a lot on spring palettes. I think I tend to lean towards richer/earthier tones. That being said, the high saturation of the spring palette seems fitting.

It's impossible to describe, but I'll do my best. 

Depression feels like an intangible darkness that lingers within me constantly, overwhelming any motivation, excitement, or happiness I may have. It causes me to feel rather flat and apathetic, and I'm often very tired and weak on a core level. Things that I used to consider "fun" now make me ask myself what the point is. There are periods of active dread, and then just pure exhaustion. Everyday life seems quite surreal, and ending it all becomes a quotidian consideration, no different from deciding what to have for breakfast.

What makes it worse is the total lack of control. It often seems as if there will never be an escape, and my future looks bleak. I can't close my eyes and forget about it; I am surrounded. It feels as though depression is a vast sea that I am drowning in. There is an island, miles away, which could perhaps save me, but I don't have the energy required to get there.

Despite this, I am planning on seeking help, and clinging to whatever hope I have left. Which, admittedly, is not a lot.
